evidence.label: Failure of rational injectivity for maximal coarse assembly
A counterexample to the coarse Novikov conjecture

headline: Graph families where coarse assembly forgets a class of infinite order; Lean checks the reduced version.
scope: Two linked papers on spaces made of finite graphs of bounded degree; Lean covers only the reduced Roe-algebra result.
plain: Coarse assembly turns large-scale shape data of a space into an index, a number-like invariant of operators. The coarse Novikov conjecture predicted that no shape class of infinite order is lost this way, even after allowing fractions. One paper proves a counterexample, with a Lean proof listed: a union of finite graphs of bounded degree. A second paper claims the same failure for the larger maximal Roe algebra.
doesNot: This does not refute coarse assembly for spaces with extra geometric conditions, such as finite asymptotic dimension or embeddings into Hilbert space.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: John Roe, coarse cohomology and coarse index theory
scorecard.significanceWhy: It refutes the rational coarse Novikov conjecture for bounded-geometry spaces, a long-standing prediction in coarse geometry.

explanation:
Start with four points on a square, joined around the edge. Neighbours are 1 step apart and opposite corners are 2 steps apart. The Rips complex at scale r fills in every group of points within distance r of each other. At scale 1 only the edges appear, so the square keeps its hole. At scale 2 all four points lie within distance 2, so the hole fills in. The loop was a real feature at one scale and nothing at a larger one. In general, a loop at one scale can bound at a larger scale[8]. Coarse geometry studies the features that survive every scale.

Coarse K-homology collects these surviving features. Coarse assembly sends each feature to an index. The index lives in the K-theory of the Roe algebra, an algebra of operators that move points only a bounded distance. The coarse Novikov conjecture asked that no feature of infinite order map to zero, even after allowing fractions. Bounded geometry means each ball of fixed radius holds a bounded number of points.

Earlier results added conditions. Yu proved assembly is an isomorphism for bounded-geometry spaces of finite asymptotic dimension[9]. He also built a kernel class for a space without bounded geometry[11]. The obstacle was to keep bounded geometry and still lose a class at every scale.

The second paper proves that the conjecture fails[7]. Begin with discs in the triangular lattice, with radius j, and their boundary loops[12]. Above each point of a disc sits a finite quotient of the matrix group SL₃(ℤ). Twisting prevents short loops from winding around the centre once j is large[14]. So the boundary loop survives as a class of infinite order. Through the filled discs, the index of that class is zero[13]. Thus bounded geometry alone is not enough[10].

The first paper claims a stronger result for the maximal Roe algebra, a larger completion of the same operators[1]. Its base graphs are three-dimensional discrete tori whose sides grow longer[4]. Over each one sits a finite quotient of SL₃(ℤ)[5]. Kazhdan's property (T), a rigidity property of that group, supplies the averaging step[6]. A zero reduced index alone does not force a zero maximal index[2]. The new class also lies in the reduced kernel[3].

How sure is this? A computer proof checker called Lean has a formal proof of the reduced counterexample. It covers the graph union, the infinite-order class and its zero index after allowing fractions. The maximal Roe algebra result is outside that check. No specialist review of either paper has been published.
hypeCheck: Major. Lean covers the reduced counterexample. The maximal version has no Lean check and no published specialist review.

glossary.meaning: A shape built from points by filling in every group of points that lie close together.
An algebraic record of the shape features of a space that survive at every large scale.
An algebra of operators that move points of the space only a bounded distance.
A map that sends each large-scale shape feature to an index in the Roe algebra's K-theory.
Every ball of a fixed radius contains at most a fixed number of points.
The largest natural completion of the bounded-distance operators.
A rigidity property of some groups that makes averaging over them behave well.
